scope: Syntactic pattern review, not error-handling scoring or business-correctness classification.

sourceReview.selection: Purposeful source review across all four projects: direct raise forms, explicit causes/suppression, conditional dispatch, context blockers, and alternate causes. Not a random sample or accuracy estimate.

cases.reviewInterpretation: Direct call-form raise wraps a lower-level failure; type and semantic correctness are unresolved.
Raising a name can denote an exception class; no constructor-call requirement or name-based defect judgment.
Conditional translation dispatch remains unresolved; individual raises are retained without path-completeness claims.
Warning emission remains unresolved; a call does not prove successful handling.
Explicit from None is recorded without a lost-context deduction.
Direct call-form raise uses a cause with the handler name spelling.
Conditional reraising and handler invocation remain unresolved; runtime dispatch is not a defect.
Nested handler retains its blocker even with explicit from None.
A qualified call-form raise without explicit from is observable; omitted from does not establish lost implicit context.
Direct PipError call with handler-name cause is a syntactic translation candidate.
Conditional SystemExit translation and bare rethrow remain unresolved.
A one-raise suite remains blocked by enclosing context-manager execution.
Name-form raise with handler-name cause is supported even without a call.
Explicit suppression of context display is recorded without grading the decision.
Nested cleanup reraises an outer name from None; raw syntax is retained, handler pattern remains blocked.
The cause is a parameter rather than the current handler binding; retained as syntax but not recognized as the handler-name pattern.
